A coding agent can connect to two different things. They are separate, and you can give it both.

| | What the agent gets | Address |
|---|---|---|
| **These docs** | The documentation, to read and search while it writes code | `https://docs.synap.live/llms.txt`, any page as `.md`, the docs MCP server at `/api/mcp` |
| **Your pod** | Your data, under the agent's own key and governance | Your pod's `/mcp`, connected with `@synap-core/cli` |

Give it the docs when it writes code against Synap (an app on the SDK, a script on the Hub REST API, an MCP
client). Connect it to your pod when it should work with your data.

## Give an agent these docs

### Start from llms.txt

[`/llms.txt`](https://docs.synap.live/llms.txt) is the entry point written for agents: the sections, the key pages,
the interfaces to prefer, and the package names that are retired and must not be used.
[`/llms-full.txt`](https://docs.synap.live/llms-full.txt) is every page in one file.

To make an agent use them in a repository, say so in its instruction file (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or a Cursor
rule):

```md
Synap documentation: https://docs.synap.live/llms.txt
Read a page as Markdown by adding .md to its URL.
```

### Every page as Markdown

Each page has a Markdown version, built from the same source as the HTML:

```bash
curl https://docs.synap.live/docs/build/agents/mcp.md                             # add .md to the URL
curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://docs.synap.live/docs/build/agents/mcp     # or ask for Markdown
```

On every page, **Copy Markdown** copies it, and **Open** sends it to ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor, or shows it on
GitHub.

### The docs MCP server

`https://docs.synap.live/api/mcp` is an MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in) with three tools:

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `list_pages` | The index of every page, with its URL |
| `get_page` | One page as Markdown, by its URL (for example `/docs/build/sdk`) |
| `search` | Full-text search over the docs |

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http synap-docs https://docs.synap.live/api/mcp
```

Cursor, in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or a project's `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "synap-docs": { "url": "https://docs.synap.live/api/mcp" }
  }
}
```

This server only serves the public documentation. It cannot see a pod.

## Connect an agent to your pod

Every pod serves its own MCP server at `/mcp`. The CLI connects an agent to it with an identity and a key of its own,
so its writes go through your pod's governance and you can revoke it separately. See
[Connect an agent](/docs/build/agents) for every client.

```bash
npx @synap-core/cli init          # first time: finds or creates your pod and connects the agents it detects
synap connect claude-code         # or: codex, cursor, claude-desktop, ...
```

- **Claude Code**: `synap connect claude-code` registers the pod's MCP server with `claude mcp add` (user scope)
  and installs the [Synap skills](/docs/build/agents/skills) in `~/.claude/skills/`.
- **Cursor**: `synap connect cursor` writes the pod's MCP server into `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.
- **claude.ai** (web): its connector settings take a URL and sign you in with OAuth, with no key to paste.
  `synap mcp connect-claude` prints the steps and the Synap Cloud URL, `https://api.synap.live/mcp`. After you
  approve, ask Claude to list your pods (`list_pods`) and connect one (`connect_pod`).

Check the connection with `synap mcp verify` and `synap whoami`.

### What the agent sees

- Tool names start with `synap_`. A new agent key lists a small entry set: `synap_orient` is the session briefing
  (what awaits your review, open work, your identity and projects), and `synap_ask` answers questions from your
  data. The agent loads more tools in groups.
  [MCP tools](/docs/reference/mcp-tools) lists them all.
- Its writes become proposals unless a rule you set lets them apply. It can never approve a proposal.
- What it may read and change is set by its key: see [API keys](/docs/build/api-keys).

## Both at once

The docs MCP server and your pod's MCP server are separate entries in the client's configuration: for example
`synap-docs`, and the `synap-<pod name>` entry that `synap connect` writes. An agent building on Synap uses the first to look up how, and the second to act on your
data.
